beats.heading: The socket owns screen presence
beats.body: Only the authoritative socket owns a pane identity. Its close removes pane and tab presence; a replaced socket cannot retire its successor.

beats.heading: News carries a version, never the board
beats.body: A board write, claim or disk change reaches the panes through announcements. The pane reads content again from the store; no pane owns a board copy.

beats.heading: Agents read the same news
beats.body: The change feed records each board broadcast and lets the workbench read changes since its cursor. Tab presence allows a reload to keep its conversation.

nodes.description: pane-arrival adopts the vault and repository that a pane_board message names, and pane-core keeps them as a mirror of the server. pane-socket opens the socket with ?vault= and socket-messages routes each message. A report is keyed by its vault, so the server answers one naming a vault the pane left with registered:false.

beats.heading: The socket owns screen presence
beats.body: Only the authoritative socket owns a pane identity. Its close removes pane and tab presence; a replaced socket cannot retire its successor.

beats.heading: News carries a version, never the board
beats.body: A board write, claim or disk change reaches the panes through announcements. The pane reads content again from the store; no pane owns a board copy.

beats.heading: Agents read the same news
beats.body: The change feed records each board broadcast and lets the workbench read changes since its cursor. Tab presence allows a reload to keep its conversation.

beats.heading: The server decides which vault a pane is in
beats.body: A show that names a pane, or a new chosen checkout of the repository it shows, moves the pane into another vault. The pane only mirrors that: it takes the vault from pane_board and names it on its socket, reports and calls. A report that names the vault it left is answered as not registered, so it cannot undo the move.

adoptions.reason: The existing seven live-pane implementations and their exchanges now have their own architecture board
Every call and pane socket names its vault: a Vault requirement refuses a call naming none, and the pane registry, board announcements and change feed keep their news per vault
The server moves a pane between vaults and tells it in pane_board, and agent activity names its vault and reaches every pane
The server serves every vault, and a pane opens in the page's opening vault
